content:
Fiber to the Home (FTTH) usually hands off the Internet signal at the optical network terminal (ONT).
From that point onward the **IP layer** is already created.
Almost all consumer FTTH providers simply plug a standard **PPPoE** session into the ONT and use **DHCPv4 or DHCPv6** to assign the public IP address and default route.
So the access protocol you actually see on your router or PC is **PPPoE over Ethernet**, even though the underlying optical transport may be GPON, XGS-PON, etc.
